title: Unit econ: add safe backfill/reprocess tooling for historical partitions (dry-run + guardrails)
author: Mei Lin
body:
Context: we need a repeatable + auditable way to reprocess unit economics datasets for historical partitions (90d backfill + occasional replays after fixing mapping/attribution bugs) without accidentally clobbering prod partitions or generating non-reconcilable totals. This PR adds a dedicated backfill CLI + job wrapper, plus documentation/runbook updates.

What’s included: (1) New CLI: `unit-econ backfill` for reprocessing historical partitions for unit-econ datasets (currently `blended_cost_daily` + semantic views dependencies). (2) Dry-run mode that prints planned actions (partitions, target tables, computed watermarks) without writing. (3) Guardrails/safety checks: requires explicit `--start`/`--end`; caps default max partitions to 31 unless `--allow-large-backfill`; blocks execution on `main` unless `--i-know-what-im-doing`; requires `--confirm` to write; validates partition existence + schema version; writes a backfill manifest row for auditability. (4) Reconciliation hooks: optional `--run-reconcile` which triggers the existing billing tie-out job after completion and fails the run if variance exceeds configured threshold. (5) Documentation: adds a runbook with common scenarios (late events spike, region mapping fixes, tier mapping corrections), expected timelines, and rollback steps.

Usage examples: `./bin/unit-econ backfill --dataset blended_cost_daily --start 2025-01-01 --end 2025-01-31 --dry-run` and `./bin/unit-econ backfill --dataset blended_cost_daily --start 2025-01-01 --end 2025-01-31 --confirm --run-reconcile`.

Operational notes: backfills write to the same canonical tables but use partition-scoped transactions and record a manifest (dataset, partition, code version, invoker, reason). By default the tool does partition-level overwrite only for the requested range; outside range is untouched. The job is idempotent for a given (dataset, partition, code version) and will no-op if the manifest indicates an identical completed run (override available with `--force`).

Why now: we’ve already needed manual replays to resolve late-arriving metering events and mapping issues (see SUP-8841), and manual SQL has been error-prone. This aligns with ENG-2918 launch criteria (90d backfill + documented process) and SRE expectations for controlled reprocessing.

Testing: unit tests for argument parsing + safety checks; integration test for manifest writes; local run against dev warehouse with dry-run + 2 partitions overwrite. CI includes lint/typecheck + pytest.

Follow-ups: (a) wire CLI into an on-demand workflow in our orchestration system (so SRE can run with approvals), (b) add support for reprocessing upstream staging tables when needed (currently assumes upstream raw is immutable).
commits: analytics(unit-econ): add backfill CLI entrypoint + argument validation
analytics(unit-econ): implement partition reprocess with manifest/audit writes
analytics(unit-econ): add dry-run planner output and max-partitions guardrail
ops(runbook): document backfill/replay procedure and reconciliation expectations
tests: add coverage for safety gates and inclusive date range behavior
conversation:
Logan Wright: Can we prevent someone from accidentally running this from a laptop against prod with a huge range? The default max partitions is good, but please add an explicit `--allow-large-backfill` flag and make it noisy in logs. Also, make sure end date is inclusive; we’ve been bitten by off-by-one in partition planners.

Mei Lin: Added `--allow-large-backfill` required for >31 partitions and updated logs to print a WARNING banner with the full partition list. Also fixed date range planning to be inclusive of `--end` and added tests.

Nadia Rahman: For overwrite semantics: do we delete then insert? We should do partition-scoped overwrite in a single transaction if possible, and write a manifest row even in dry-run (marked as planned) so we can audit intent.

Mei Lin: Implemented partition-scoped overwrite via `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` and moved manifest to two states: PLANNED for dry-run (no writes to target tables) and COMPLETED for real runs. Dry-run manifest is optional behind `--record-plan` because Finance asked to avoid writing anything on dry-run in prod.

Cole Summers: If `--run-reconcile` fails, do we revert partitions? I’d rather fail the run and leave partitions written than attempt rollback (warehouse rollback is not reliable across long runs). But we should print a clear next-step and link to the reconciliation doc.

Mei Lin: Agree—no automatic rollback. Added failure output that includes the variance numbers + link to runbook section “Reconcile failures”.

Allison Grant: Please add a metric + structured log event for backfill runs (dataset, partitions count, duration, result) so oncall can correlate with freshness alerts. Also ensure the tool writes to #eng-platform only when it actually writes.

Mei Lin: Added `unit_econ_backfill_run_total` + `unit_econ_backfill_run_duration_seconds` metrics and structured logs. Slack notification only fires on non-dry-run with `--confirm`.

Aisha Bello: Documentation request: include a checklist for running in prod (dry-run first, limit partitions, run reconcile, post in channel, annotate incident if relevant). Also call out late-event cutoff behavior.

Mei Lin: Added a checklist + a note about late-event cutoff: we reprocess full partitions; late events beyond 7 days can still shift totals, and reconcile will catch variances.

CI: First run failed due to lint (unused import) and a flaky integration test. Mei reran after fix; green.

Approvals: Logan Wright approved; Nadia Rahman approved; Allison Grant approved.

Merged via squash.
release_notes: Added a supported backfill/reprocess tool for unit economics historical partitions with dry-run and safety checks.
Backfill runs now emit audit manifests and optional reconciliation failures for faster investigation.
